_authoring.source: Season 1 Script Bible + episode_01.json, Creative Director. Spine and all authored lines are his; branch responses under `responses` are expanded for the web build.
_authoring.fizRule: Fiz never speaks in a dialogue_sequence. His spoken lines exist only inside choices, where the player picks them.
_authoring.choiceKinds: "Quoted" = spoken aloud. [Bracketed] = an action, or a pointed silence. The engine detects which from the text; do not add a field.
_authoring.responses: Keyed by consequence_id. Plays immediately after the choice, then the sequence reconverges. Any line that only makes sense after one specific option must live in `responses`, never in the shared trunk.
_authoring.neverTerminal: Every scene ends on a dialogue entry, never on a choice block.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Four hours. The ceiling has a water stain shaped like an island. Some mornings it's Java. Some mornings it's nothing.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (One year today. Nobody's going to say it. That's fine. That's the deal.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
dialogue_sequence.text: Fiz. I can hear your alarm through the wall. It's been going for eleven minutes.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
dialogue_sequence.text: I'm not gonna write you up. I'm just gonna stand here judging you until you turn it off.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (She does this. Checks on me like I'm something she's responsible for. I don't know how to tell her that helps.)

choices.choice_text: "You've been up since five, haven't you."

gina_accepts_apology.speaker: Gina Ortiz
gina_accepts_apology.text: You're not up. You're vertical. Those are different things and I've seen both.

gina_lingers_at_door.speaker: Gina Ortiz
gina_lingers_at_door.text: Right. We're doing the one where you don't answer and I fill in your half myself.

gina_lingers_at_door.speaker: Gina Ortiz
gina_lingers_at_door.text: Fine. I'll assume you said, 'Morning, Gina, you're doing a great job and nobody appreciates you.'

gina_deflects_own_exhaustion.speaker: Gina Ortiz
gina_deflects_own_exhaustion.text: ...Four-forty. Room check, laundry room flooded again, then somebody crying in 3B for an hour.

gina_deflects_own_exhaustion.speaker: Gina Ortiz
gina_deflects_own_exhaustion.text: Don't do that. Don't turn it around on me. I'm the one with the clipboard, that's the whole system.

gina_deflects_own_exhaustion.speaker: Fiz
gina_deflects_own_exhaustion.text: (She's smiling at the doorframe. She does that when somebody gets it right and she'd rather not say so.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Gina Ortiz
dialogue_sequence.text: Hall check's in ten. And Fiz — eat something today. Not the vending machine. Something with a shape.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Headphones. Aura. The Strokes. The same song I've played four hundred times because it's the only thing that makes the noise in my head line up straight.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Somewhere between the door and the stairs my brain runs the thing again. A hallway. Someone raising a gun. Me, calm. Always calm, in the version where it happens.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Nobody's ever raised anything at me. My head just likes rehearsing.)

camera_acquired_flag.speaker: Fiz
camera_acquired_flag.text: (Four hundred and six grams. I know because I weighed it once, at two in the morning, for no reason I could give anyone.)

camera_left_behind_flag.speaker: Fiz
camera_left_behind_flag.text: (It sits there on the desk being looked at instead of looking.)

camera_left_behind_flag.speaker: Fiz
camera_left_behind_flag.text: (I get four steps down the stairwell before the wrongness of it starts up behind my ribs. I keep walking anyway. That's the experiment.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Down the stairs. Out through the double doors. One year to the day since I first came the other way through them, with a suitcase and a printed map of a town that had already stopped existing once.)

meta.weather: Rain easing off the coast road.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz

dialogue_sequence.text: You know this place used to be packed at seven? Line out the door. Fishermen, truckers, half the school skipping first period.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz

marcus_declines_to_answer.text: Didn't say it was a problem.

marcus_declines_to_answer.speaker: Marcus Islah
marcus_declines_to_answer.text: Said I know what mud looks like.

marcus_doesnt_take_it.speaker: Fiz
marcus_doesnt_take_it.text: (I hold it out. He doesn't take it. He doesn't even look down at it.)

marcus_doesnt_take_it.speaker: Marcus Islah
marcus_doesnt_take_it.text: Put that away. I'm not a cop any more, and between us, I wasn't a good one.

marcus_respects_the_silence.speaker: Fiz
marcus_respects_the_silence.text: (Eleven seconds. He's better at this than I am and we both know it by about second four.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Marcus Islah
dialogue_sequence.text: Kid. I'm not confiscating anything. I've never confiscated anything off you and I've had eleven chances.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Marcus Islah
dialogue_sequence.text: Careful where you point that thing.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Not a threat. I've been threatened. This was the other thing.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
dialogue_sequence.text: Rowe left the lab key with me. Don't tell anyone, he'll stop doing it.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
dialogue_sequence.text: You cutting the lighthouse stuff? I'll shut up. I know you don't like people over your shoulder.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Two hours. The good kind. The kind where the noise finally has somewhere to go.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Clip four. The wide of the ruins. I've watched it eleven times because something in it keeps pulling my eye and I can't name what.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (There. Timecode 00:04:41. Fog rolling left to right across the frame.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Then, for eleven frames — less than half a second — it rolls right to left. Same fog. Same shot. No cut.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I step it frame by frame. There's no seam. No dropped frames. The timecode doesn't skip. It's continuous footage and the weather goes backwards inside it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
dialogue_sequence.text: You've gone grey, man. What.

jamie_sees_something_else.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
jamie_sees_something_else.text: ...I mean. Codec's doing something weird? Interlacing, maybe. Cheap sensor in fog, it happens, I've seen it happen.

jamie_sees_something_else.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
jamie_sees_something_else.text: That's not — that's not what that is, is it.

jamie_sees_something_else.speaker: Fiz
jamie_sees_something_else.text: (He's giving me a rational answer. He's giving it to himself, really.)

jamie_sees_something_else.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
jamie_sees_something_else.text: My sister was a student here. In 2013.

jamie_sees_something_else.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
jamie_sees_something_else.text: I'm not saying those are related. I'm saying I'm going home now.

jamie_lets_it_go.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
jamie_lets_it_go.text: You've got the face people make when it isn't a bad export, but okay.

jamie_lets_it_go.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
jamie_lets_it_go.text: I'll be over there. Not looking. Obviously not looking.

jamie_lets_it_go.speaker: Fiz
jamie_lets_it_go.text: (He goes back to his own timeline and doesn't cut a single frame for twenty minutes.)

anomaly_kept_private.speaker: Fiz
anomaly_kept_private.text: (The lid goes down. Jamie doesn't ask again.)

anomaly_kept_private.speaker: Jamie Vaughn
anomaly_kept_private.text: For what it's worth — if you ever do want somebody to look at something, I'm quite good, and I don't talk.

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (Out in the corridor the lights are already off. Somewhere below, a door closes on its own weight.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (2:14 AM. I've watched it ninety times. It doesn't get less true.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (There are four rational explanations. I've tested three. The fourth is that I'm wrong about what I'm seeing, which is the one I'd like, so I don't trust it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (A year of being polite. A year of not asking. Linda changing the subject. Riley stepping back from the water. Marcus saying careful. Sienna taking it back before anyone made her.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I thought this town was quiet. It isn't quiet. It's holding its breath.)

choices.choice_text: [Back it up three times. Tell no one. Start looking.]
[Delete it. Go to sleep. Be a guest here.]

ep1_end_tell_riley.speaker: Fiz
ep1_end_tell_riley.text: (Sent. 2:19 AM. The three dots start almost immediately, which means she was awake too, which means she's been awake all week.)

ep1_end_tell_riley.speaker: Fiz
ep1_end_tell_riley.text: (Then: don't do anything until I'm there.)

ep1_end_go_alone.speaker: Fiz
ep1_end_go_alone.text: (Three copies. Two drives and a folder with a boring name, buried where nobody looks for interesting things.)

ep1_end_go_alone.speaker: Fiz
ep1_end_go_alone.text: (This is the part of the story where a smarter person tells somebody.)

ep1_end_delete.speaker: Fiz
ep1_end_delete.text: (Deleted. Emptied. Then I sat there looking at the empty folder for a length of time I'd rather not write down.)

ep1_end_delete.speaker: Fiz
ep1_end_delete.text: (The backup drive is still plugged in. I didn't touch it. I also didn't unplug it.)

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: ("I guess if bad shit happens I should just let it happen.")

dialogue_sequence.speaker: Fiz
dialogue_sequence.text: (I've been telling myself that for a year. Tonight it sounds like something a coward says.)
